feeds_status:
**THE ideas-feeds ACTION HAS NOW LANDED NOTHING FOR FOUR CONSECUTIVE TRADING DAYS (13, 16, 17 and 18 November) AND THIS IS THE BIGGEST PROBLEM IN THE PIPELINE.** `docs/ideas/feeds_status.json` still carries `built` **2026-11-12 19:57 IST** (run 43227180887), which was the last successful run.

Measured from the Actions API in this run, not inferred:

| run | date | started → ended (UTC) | wall | conclusion |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 43227180887 | 2026-11-12 | 13:25:38 → 14:27:34 | 62 min | **success** |
| 43433543004 | 2026-11-13 | 13:25:38 → 14:56:02 | 90 min | cancelled |
| 43875640839 | 2026-11-16 | 13:25:39 → 14:56:02 | 90 min | cancelled |
| 44092608136 | 2026-11-17 | 13:25:39 → 14:56:04 | 90 min | cancelled |
| 44313598476 | 2026-11-18 | 13:25:40 → still in_progress when checked at 14:08 UTC | — | on the same path |

**The cause, from run 44092608136's own step timings.** Steps 1–18 ALL succeeded — the host probe, the PIB government lane, every commodity host, WPI, trade, universe, the scan, signals and the scorecard were done by 13:48:52Z, 23 minutes in. Then **step 19 "Order-book ledger refresh" ran 13:48:52Z → 14:50:09Z — 61 minutes on its own** — and step 20 "Breakout watch" was cancelled mid-run at 14:55:53Z when the job hit its 90-minute cap. Steps 21–24 (order wins, ob_tracker, the filings queue, the status guard) were skipped, and so was step 26 **"Commit the feeds"**. Nothing was committed on any of the three cancelled days.

**Why that matters more than it looks.** The routine's own sandbox cannot reach PIB at all, so Actions is the only reader of the government lane. Three cancelled runs read PIB successfully and threw the result away. The government lane has therefore been dark since 2026-11-12 — six calendar days — and `orderbook_signals.json`, `orderwins_signals.json`, `govt.json` and `spot.json` all still carry the 11-12 build.

**The fix is a workflow change this routine is not allowed to make** (the prompt scopes it to `docs/ideas/` and forbids editing `scripts/ideas/*.py`; `.github/workflows/ideas-feeds.yml` is outside both). Three options, cheapest first: (a) raise the job's `timeout-minutes` above 90 — the successful 11-12 run took 62 min, so the margin is thin and a slow BSE day will keep tripping it; (b) move "Order-book ledger refresh" into its own scheduled workflow so it cannot starve the commit step; (c) move the commit step so that whatever HAS been built lands even when a later step is killed — which is the real defect, since steps 1–18 produced a complete day's feeds every single time.

`landing.refused` was empty on the last successful run, so nothing was lost to a same-path commit race.

orderbook_jumps_table:
**One new row, checked against both source documents this run, and it is a misread — recorded so it is never checked again.**

`docs/ideas/orderbook_jumps.json` went from 51 to **52 rows** (built 2026-11-18 21:05 IST). The new row is **Admach Systems Ltd (BSE 544669, mcap ₹378 cr)**, which the refreshed screen showed at ₹51.44 cr → ₹78.39 cr, **+52.4%**.

**The latest figure is fully CONFIRMED.** The 14-Nov-2026 press release states *"Current Order Book: ₹78.39 Crore (including GST)"* in its key highlights and the MD repeats it in his quote — and the covering letter's own subject line is *"Submission of Press Release pertaining to Total Order Book of the Company"*, so it is unambiguously the company-wide total rather than a segment or an L1 position. The filing itself is a ₹97.04 lakh NDT X-ray cabinet order from an unnamed domestic customer, 16-week execution.

**The year-ago figure is the right number on the wrong date, and that kills the comparison.** ₹51.44 cr is real — but the document it comes from is the 31-Dec-2025 press release announcing a ₹10.62 cr Nuclear Fuel Complex order, and the figure sits in that release's *"About Admach Systems Limited"* boilerplate: *"In FY25, the Company reported revenue of ₹5,335.82 lakhs, EBITDA of ₹1,030.91 lakhs, and PAT of ₹609.81 lakhs, supported by strong return ratios and a growing order book of approx. ₹5,144 lakhs."* Three defects follow:

1. **The as-on date is misdated by the screen.** `orderbook.py` assigned 2025-09-30 using its 'quarter before filing' rule. The sentence attaches the figure to **FY25**, i.e. the year ended 31-Mar-2025. That makes the span 31-Mar-2025 → 14-Nov-2026 = **594 days**, about 19.5 months, outside the 240–480 day window the rule intends.
2. **On the correct dates it is not a jump.** +52.4% over 19.5 months is roughly **+30% a year**, below the 50% bar.
3. **The two figures are not stated on the same basis.** ₹78.39 cr is explicitly 'including GST'; the ₹5,144 lakh figure states no GST basis, is qualified 'approx.', and is boilerplate rather than an order-book disclosure.

Verdict **NOT A JUMP**, `qualifies: false`, `true_yoy_pct: null`. For context the ₹78.39 cr book is **0.95x** trailing revenue of ₹82.66 cr (H2 FY26 + H1 FY27, measured from this company's own filings for its published card 2026-10-27-ADMACH), and the FY25 book of ~₹51.44 cr was 0.96x that year's ₹53.36 cr. A row was also appended to `docs/ideas/orderbook_verified.json` (45 → **46 rows**) with `latest_verdict: CORRECT` and `year_ago_verdict: WRONG DATE`.

**A fetch detail worth recording:** the year-ago PDF is no longer on `AttachLive` — that URL returns BSE's "The Page you are looking for has been moved" HTML, which PyMuPDF happily parses as a two-page document of navigation links. It had to be re-fetched from `AttachHis`. Any check that reads an older filing by its stored AttachLive URL will silently get an error page instead of the document; the giveaway is a suspiciously small file (8 KB here) or body text about 'Pre Open / Equity Market Watch'.

`scripts/ideas/ob_tracker.py` was then re-run (21:14 IST): **34 qualifying jump rows priced, 0 carried forward stale**, plus **25 order-wins rows priced, 0 stale**. It also rewrote `docs/ideas/orderwins_tracker.json`, which is committed alongside. Admach is not in the tracker because `qualifies` is false, which is correct.

updates_sweep:
**THE QUEUE COULD NOT BE REBUILT FROM THIS SANDBOX, AND SAYING SO IS THE HONEST HEADLINE: `docs/ideas/updates_queue.json` IS STILL THE 2026-11-13 21:04 IST BUILD, FIVE DAYS OLD AND COVERING 80 IDEAS, NOT TODAY'S 86.** It also still carries `second_reader_misses: 1` with `second_reader_problems: ['BSE daily list 2026-11-13 incomplete']` from that build. The sweep below was therefore done WITHOUT a current queue, by a reader built in this run, and the gap it cannot close is named at the end.

**Why the queue could not be rebuilt — read from updates.py itself, not inferred.** `www.nseindia.com` answers **403** at this sandbox's egress proxy (`nsearchives.nseindia.com` answers, the API host does not), so every per-company NSE read fails. The script guards exactly this case:

    if NSE_CALLS['ok'] == 0 and NSE_CALLS['fail'] > 0:
        print('NSE UNREACHABLE: ... updates_queue.json LEFT UNCHANGED ...'); sys.exit(3)

The write is **after** that guard, so a run from here can never produce a queue — by design, because a queue built without NSE would silently drop every NSE-only filing. The committed queue is supposed to come from the ideas-feeds Action, which reaches NSE; that Action has not committed for four trading days (see `feeds_status`). **So this is the same single root cause as the government lane, not a separate problem.**

**A process error of this run, stated because it cost time and should not be repeated.** `updates.py --selftest` was started at 19:53 IST wrapped in `timeout 5400`, and the timeout killed it at **idea 55 of 83** (RC=124) just before `2026-10-21-ORIRAIL`. Nothing was lost but the time: the queue write and the SELFTEST assertions both run only after all 83 ideas are read, so a killed run leaves no output at all — **and no SELFTEST verdict was obtained in this run, which the playbook requires.** It was restarted detached at 21:24 IST and then **deliberately stopped** once the exit-3 guard above was read: a second 1.5-hour pass could not have written the queue either. The lesson for the prompt: on this sandbox `updates.py` is a ~2.5-hour job that cannot succeed at all, so it should be run only to harvest its per-idea read, or skipped in favour of the committed queue.

**What the killed pass did measure, over its 55 ideas:** **40 came back SUSPECT and 15 complete**, every SUSPECT being `NSE <window> failed`. 19 filings were flagged `new since 2026-11-17`. So for every NSE-listed idea the queue would have been BSE-only.

**The gap reader built in this run, and what it found.** Since BSE answered all evening, a throwaway reader was written in the scratchpad (not in `scripts/ideas/`, which this routine must not edit) that takes BSE's **whole-market day lists for 2026-11-14 to 2026-11-18** — already cached complete by the scan and the order-book refresh, each with `rows` equal to BSE's own `reported` count (2,326 / 239 / 1,073 / 755 / 646) — and matches every row to our ideas by BSE scrip code:

|---|---:|
| ideas with a BSE scrip (visible to this reader) | **74 of 86** |
| BSE filings matched, 14–18 Nov | **110** |
| of those, non-routine | **95** |

researched.name: INDO SMC Ltd
researched.reason: Top of the scan at score 9. Two filings today: a ₹18.25 cr purchase order (₹1,825.20 lakh ex-tax, 120-day delivery, for feeder/mini section pillars, switch-fuse units and FRP fencing) and the transcript of the 16-Nov Q2/H1 FY27 call. **The order is NOT the reason it was published, and the card says so**: ₹18.25 cr is 4.4% of ₹413.30 cr of trailing-year revenue — the under-10%-of-sales bucket, 21.4% odds of 2x in two years against 35.7% for a 25–50% order — and INDO SMC has filed EIGHT purchase-order intimations in 240 days, which is the serial-bidder bucket (17.3% to 2x, never 5x). It was published for what the transcript and the 3-Nov results filing contain: H1 FY27 revenue ₹216.10 cr (+92.0% YoY) and PAT ₹20.18 cr (+76.1%); explicit multi-year guidance of ₹450 cr FY27 / ₹600–700 cr FY28 / ~₹1,000 cr FY29 at a 10–11% PAT margin, reaffirmed on the call; MSEDCL vendor approval for 11 kV and 33 kV isolators with 33 kV metering cubicles in final approval; a ~60,000 sq ft Nashik block said to be a month from working and worth ₹200–300 cr at 80%; and a stock down 36.6% in three months against all of that. **Three things are stated as plainly as the growth**: half-on-half PAT is DOWN 3.6% (₹20.18 cr vs ₹20.93 cr in H2 FY26) and EBITDA margin is down 311 bps to 12.69%; the MD admitted persistently negative operating cash flow on the record, targeting positive "by next Diwali"; and the ₹145 cr order book at 31-Oct is 0.35x trailing sales and covers only 70% of the ₹233.9 cr H2 that the ₹450 cr guidance needs. A transformer plant fundraise is flagged as likely dilution. Ownership is the strongest verified fact: Ashish Kacholia has ADDED in each of the last two quarters — 2.46% (Mar-26) → 3.03% (Jun-26) → 3.25% (Sep-26) — read from the three BSE shareholding XBRL filings in this run.

researched.name: Glen Industries Ltd
researched.reason: Scan score 6. H1 FY27 total income ₹116.47 cr (+20.6%) and PAT ₹10.91 cr (+31.4%), PAT margin +77 bps to 9.37% — but profit outgrew revenue because interest and depreciation both FELL in absolute terms while EBITDA margin slipped 141 bps, so the card calls it a balance-sheet improvement rather than an operating one. Published mainly because it is the one name today where the physical model actually closes on the company's own numbers: thin-wall container production of 3,133 MT in H1 against 665 MT/month × 6 = 3,990 MT of capacity is **78.5% utilisation**, and TWC at 80.75% of ₹115.30 cr of revenue implies a realisation of **₹2.97 lakh/MT**. Both internally consistent. Guidance is primary-sourced from the 29-May-2026 analyst meet: FY28 ₹500+ cr with EBITDA ₹90+ cr, built as ₹200–215 cr from existing capacity plus ~₹300 cr from the new Howrah plant (capex raised to ₹130–133 cr from ~₹100 cr). **The bad half is today's third filing and it is the core of the card**: a project update dated 28-Oct and filed today moves commercial production to Q4 FY27, after Q4 FY26 in the prospectus and then Q3 FY27 — which removes most of the ₹100–125 cr FY27 contribution management guided in May, and no revised FY27 number has been given. note:
**THREE CARDS FROM THE FILINGS LANE, AND FOR THE FOURTH RUN RUNNING THE DAY'S REAL STORY IS THAT THE FEED PIPELINE DID NOT RUN.** The `ideas-feeds` Action has now been cancelled at its 90-minute job cap on 13, 16 and 17 November and today's run 44313598476 was still in_progress on the same path when this run checked it. Every time, steps 1–18 finished successfully inside 23 minutes — PIB, every commodity host, WPI, trade, universe, the scan, signals, the scorecard — and every time step 19 'Order-book ledger refresh' then ran for about an hour and the job was killed before step 26 'Commit the feeds'. So a complete day's feeds was built and discarded three times. The fix is in `.github/workflows/ideas-feeds.yml`, which this routine is scoped out of; the three options are set out in `feeds_status`, and the one that matters most is moving the commit so that what HAS been built lands even when a later step is killed.

**This run did the order-book refresh itself, which is the thing the Action cannot finish.** `orderbook.py --refresh` was started at 19:45 IST and allowed to run to completion rather than being abandoned as it was yesterday — a cloud session has no 90-minute cap. The result is in `orderbook_lane` and `orderbook_jumps_table`.

**Lane by lane.** GOVERNMENT: nothing, and that is a failure rather than a quiet day — PIB has been unreadable from this sandbox for eight consecutive attempted days and the Action that can read it threw away three successful reads. COMMODITY: 37 of 53 groups above the bar but **no price print newer than 2026-11-12**, so no commodity idea was published; the two standing signals that matter were used as documented red flags on today's cards instead (crude/resin against Glen and BLS Polymers, copper and crude against INDO SMC's 311 bps of margin compression). FILING: 15 candidates, four opened to their filings, three published.

**What the three cards have in common is that the trigger the scan fired on is not the reason any of them was published.** INDO SMC's ₹18.25 cr order is 4.4% of a trailing year's sales from a company that has filed eight order intimations in 240 days — both of the weak buckets in the measured order study — so the card says plainly that the order is a routine data point in a monthly cadence and the reasons to look are the H1 results, the reaffirmed ₹450/₹600–700/₹1,000 cr guidance, and a 36.6% three-month drawdown. Glen's results look better than they are (profit outgrew revenue only because interest and depreciation fell; EBITDA margin slipped 141 bps) and the most important filing of its day was the project update that slipped the Howrah plant a third time, to Q4 FY27, removing most of the ₹100–125 cr FY27 contribution management guided in May. BLS Polymers has the best business of the three on every return and cash metric and is published at LOW confidence anyway, because eleven trading sessions of listed life, no transcript, no annual report, no guidance, no disclosed utilisation, no disclosed pass-through and no comparable peer is not enough evidence to carry 51x trailing earnings at an all-time high.

**One ownership fact was worth the whole X sweep:** Ashish Kacholia has added to INDO SMC in each of the last two quarters — 2.46% in Mar-2026, 3.03% in Jun-2026, 3.25% in Sep-2026 — read from the three BSE shareholding XBRL filings in this run. The X posts that pointed at him all described it as a new position; the filings show it is an accumulation.

**And one defect in this routine's own setup, fixed here but worth fixing in the prompt:** step 0's pymupdf install goes to Python 3.13 while `python3` is 3.11.18, so `import fitz` still failed and `minsteel.py` crashed. Use `python3 -m pip install --quiet pymupdf xlrd`.
data_problems: **THE ideas-feeds ACTION HAS COMMITTED NOTHING FOR FOUR TRADING DAYS AND THIS IS THE SINGLE BIGGEST PROBLEM IN THE PIPELINE.** Runs 43433543004 (13-Nov), 43875640839 (16-Nov) and 44092608136 (17-Nov) were each cancelled at exactly 90 minutes; run 44313598476 (18-Nov) was still in_progress at 14:08 UTC on the same path. In every cancelled run steps 1–18 SUCCEEDED (host probe, PIB government lane, every commodity host, WPI, trade, universe, scan, signals, scorecard) and were done 23 minutes in; step 19 'Order-book ledger refresh' then ran 61 minutes (13:48:52Z → 14:50:09Z on 17-Nov) and step 20 'Breakout watch' was cancelled mid-step, so steps 21–24 and step 26 'Commit the feeds' were skipped. Last successful commit: `feeds_status.json` built 2026-11-12 19:57 IST. **Needs a change to `.github/workflows/ideas-feeds.yml`, which this routine is not permitted to touch** — raise `timeout-minutes` above 90 (the successful 11-12 run took 62 min, so the margin is thin), and/or split the order-book refresh into its own workflow, and/or move the commit step earlier so a day's completed feeds land even when a later step is killed.

**THE GOVERNMENT LANE HAS BEEN DARK SINCE 2026-11-12 — SIX CALENDAR DAYS.** `govt.py` could not reach pib.gov.in for 18, 17, 16, 15, 14, 13, 12 or 11 November; every attempt was `Tunnel connection failed: 403 Forbidden` at the sandbox egress proxy, which is the sandbox allowlist and not PIB refusing us. The builder behaved correctly — `govt.json` was left untouched at its 2026-11-12 18:57 IST build and the eight days are recorded as UNREAD for retry. The compounding problem is that Actions CAN read PIB and did so successfully on 13, 16 and 17 November, but all three runs were cancelled before committing. So the lane is not blocked in one place; it is blocked in the sandbox and discarded in Actions.

**EVERY COMMODITY PRICE SOURCE EXCEPT THE BSE-HOSTED ONES WAS BLOCKED FROM THIS SANDBOX, SO THE PANEL CARRIES NO PRICE NEWER THAN 2026-11-12.** `spot.py`: all 8 westmetall series and businessinsider failed, 0 commodities fetched, `spot.json` and `spot_series.json` LEFT UNCHANGED (correct behaviour). `india_spot.py`: metalbook, ibja, rubber, sugar, fuel, cai, spices, guidechem and trading-economics all FAILED with 'previous rows kept'; only `nmdc` (2 rows), `minsteel` (3 rows, re-published from the committed file) and `moil` (3 rows) worked, all three being BSE-hosted. **0 history rows appended.** `india_history.json.gz` WAS rebuilt — 275 series, 80,960 dated points — so the price-history charts are intact. `minsteel.py`: steel.gov.in unreachable, no report listed, committed file left as it was. `wpi.py`: eaindustry.nic.in unreachable, `wpi.json.gz` LEFT UNCHANGED. `trade.py --latest`: tradestat.commerce.gov.in unreachable, `trade/*` LEFT UNCHANGED. Consequence for the lane: `spot_date` 2026-11-12 (four trading days stale, past the three-day line), `trade_month` 2026-08, and `wpi_month` **2026-04, which is seven months old**. The WPI evidence behind the top three signals (Crude oil, Silver, Sulphuric acid) has not moved since April and must not be read as a new move.

**THE X SWEEP COULD NOT READ A SINGLE POST DIRECTLY.** `cdn.syndication.twimg.com:443` was refused at the egress proxy (`connect_rejected`), so the playbook's method — fetch a post by id and read its `text` / `note_tweet` JSON — was unavailable for all three researched names. Every gist in every `x_posts` entry and every quote in every `social` section is taken from a domain-restricted WebSearch snippet, which is weaker evidence; each card says so in its own words. WebSearch itself worked, and the sweep still produced 12 primary-verified data points and 2 contradictions, so this degraded the sweep rather than stopping it.

**THE VALUEPICKR SWEEP DID NOT RUN AT ALL.** `forum.valuepickr.com:443` was refused at the egress proxy (`connect_rejected`), so neither `search.json?q=` nor `raw/<id>?page=N` was reachable for any name. A domain-restricted WebSearch over forum.valuepickr.com was used instead and found no dedicated thread for INDO SMC, Glen Industries or BLS Polymers — but it did find BLS Polymers named in passing inside the DDev Plastiks Industries thread, which **could not be opened to check for more**. All three cards record this as 'not checked properly', never as 'nothing on ValuePickr'.

**THE SCAN'S FILING COUNT IS A FLOOR, NOT THE DAY.** `announcements_total` 613 against BSE's own `announcements_reported` 619, so `announcements_capped` is TRUE: one page came back six rows short and the rows kept are the newest. The read was at 19:44 IST, i.e. same-day, so filings uploaded after that are absent — BLS Polymers' own results came in at 18:45–19:20 IST and only just made it. Never quote 613 as the day's filings.

**THE ORDER-BOOK AND ORDER-WINS SCREENS WERE STALE WHEN THE RUN STARTED, FOR THE SAME ROOT CAUSE.** `orderbook_signals.json` and `orderwins_signals.json` both carried the 2026-11-12 build. This run refreshed the order-book ledger itself (see `orderbook_lane`); `order_wins.py` was deliberately NOT re-run because it needs the NSE whole-market day lists and `www.nseindia.com` answers 403 from this sandbox, so a run here would read half the market and could only remove rows.

**A DEFECT IN THIS ROUTINE'S OWN STEP 0.** `python3 -c "import fitz" 2>/dev/null || pip install --quiet pymupdf` cannot work on this image: `pip` belongs to Python 3.13 and `python3` on PATH is 3.11.18, so pymupdf 2.1 and xlrd installed into `/usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages` while `import fitz` kept failing under 3.11 — pip even reported 'Requirement already satisfied' on the retry. `minsteel.py` crashed with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fitz'`. Fixed in-run with `python3 -m pip install --quiet pymupdf xlrd`; the prompt's step 0 should use `python3 -m pip` so a future run does not read this as 'PDF reading unavailable'. (Note also that PyMuPDF 2.1 warns `fitz` is deprecated in favour of `import pymupdf` — that is a future break for every builder here, not a current one.)

**THE SHIP-IT PAGE GATE COULD ONLY BE RUN HALFWAY, AND IT CAUGHT THREE REAL DEFECTS ANYWAY.** `docs/ideas.html` is auth-gated and renders 'This page is private' without Supabase, which is blocked from this sandbox, so the cards could not be seen rendered in a browser. Instead `md()`, `inl()`, `esc()` and `table()` were extracted from `docs/ideas.html` itself and the three cards' markdown was run through the real implementations under Node. That found and fixed: three lines where a blockquote-to-bold conversion had nested `*` inside `*` (which renders as literal asterisks), and one `*Audited\*` escape that left a stray `*`. Final pass: 100,046 rendered characters, 46 tables, 958 cells, every markdown link resolved to an anchor, no stray pipes, no unclosed bold, no literal `>` (md() has no blockquote support), nothing unsafe — **0 defects**. All 27 `docs/ideas/*.json` files and both `.json.gz` files were verified to parse. What was NOT verified: the cards' appearance, dark/light rendering and 375px layout in a real browser.
